summaries.information_need: An analyst studying the Bitcoin halving cycle needs to characterize its recurring bull market, bear market, and stagnation phases, including the typical sequence of drawdowns and recoveries that mark the boundaries of a full cycle, in order to anchor later volatility analysis to cycle stage.

summaries.field: cryptocurrency finance / safe haven and hedge analysis
summaries.information_need: An analyst wants to know whether Bitcoin price movement that is driven by the halving cycle and independent of stock market swings satisfies the negative correlation condition required to classify an asset as a safe haven or hedge, and under what circumstances that condition might or might not hold.
summaries.answer_type: empirical test of a classification condition

summaries.field: cryptocurrency finance / market structure and adoption
summaries.information_need: An analyst wants to gauge how growing institutional and industrial adoption, including exchange traded fund launches, corporate treasury purchases, and expanding mining capacity, might change Bitcoin's risk profile and its plausibility as an investable or hedging asset going forward, especially given the market's rapid pace of capital inflow.

A risk manager assessing Bitcoin tail risk with value at risk is concerned that a single regime volatility model ignoring regime changes will understate risk during calm periods that precede a shock, and wants to know when this bias matters and how regimes relate to the conditional variance process.

summaries.field: cryptocurrency finance / safe haven and hedge analysis
summaries.information_need: An analyst comparing Bitcoin against gold as competing safe haven and hedge candidates against equity downturns needs to reconcile the mixed prior evidence on whether Bitcoin behaves like digital gold, and under what market conditions either asset actually provides diversification benefit.

A researcher setting up an empirical test of hedge properties across assets needs to know how the daily return dataset was constructed, which stock indices and price sources were used, and how the sample period was split to compare behavior before and after a market shock.

summaries.field: cryptocurrency finance / safe haven and hedge analysis
summaries.information_need: An analyst needs the regression specification used to classify a candidate asset as a weak or strong safe haven or hedge, including how dummy variables for extreme downside stock movements at different quantiles enter the model and how the resulting coefficients determine the classification.

An analyst wants to extend the hedge regression so the sensitivity of a hedge asset to stock market moves can differ across two threshold defined regimes rather than being forced into one global relationship, and wants to see how such a regime switching regression is specified.

A modeler building a Markov switching GARCH model for Bitcoin needs the specification choices involved, including symmetric versus asymmetric conditional variance equations, the number of regimes to allow, how regime duration is estimated, and how the model is fitted and selected against a single regime benchmark.

An analyst wants to know whether a regime switching volatility model forecasts value at risk out of sample more accurately than a single regime model, verified through coverage based backtests that check whether the predicted risk level is exceeded at the expected rate.

An analyst preparing a multi asset return series for volatility modeling needs descriptive statistics and a stationarity test to characterize its basic distributional properties, such as mean return, volatility, skewness, kurtosis, and risk adjusted return, before fitting a time series model.

summaries.field: cryptocurrency finance / safe haven and hedge analysis
summaries.information_need: An analyst wants to compare whether gold and Bitcoin actually behaved as a safe haven or hedge against major stock indices before versus after an extreme market downturn, based on the sign and significance of the estimated hedge regression coefficients in each period, indicating hedge effectiveness or its absence.

summaries.field: cryptocurrency finance / safe haven and hedge analysis
summaries.information_need: An analyst wants to track how the correlation between a candidate hedge asset and the stock market shifts from one period to the next across major indices, since the sign and stability of that correlation underpins whether the asset can be relied on as a hedge going forward.

An analyst wants to test whether Bitcoin's conditional variance process contains regime changes, meaning statistically distinct volatility regimes, across its full price history, as groundwork before comparing a regime switching specification against a single regime benchmark, using the full observation window rather than a subsample.

A modeler who has fitted competing single and two regime GARCH and GJR specifications wants to know which one best matches the data, and how persistent and distinct the estimated regimes are, in terms of their volatility level, transition probability, and expected duration.

An analyst wants to know what the detected regime changes in Bitcoin volatility actually correspond to, whether they track the bull, bear, and stagnation stages of the halving cycle or instead simply reflect low versus high volatility periods independent of cycle stage, and whether this finding should hold beyond the sample studied.
